title: Quasi-compactness and coherent finite coproducts in a sheaf topos
statement: Let $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be the category of sheaves of sets on a small site $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], in the containing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Quasi-compact, quasi-separated and coherent objects have the meanings of [def-trf-coherent-topos]; no coherence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is imposed. Every finite coproduct of coherent objects is coherent. Moreover, if $B$ is quasi-compact and $B\to\coprod_{i\in I}A_i$ is a map with $I$ finite, then each $B\times_{\coprod_i A_i}A_i$ is quasi-compact. These finite-family assertions include $I=\varnothing$ and the initial sheaf.

proof.text: By the empty-coproduct clause of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus], the initial sheaf $0$ is quasi-compact. For maps $B,C\to0$, strictness of $0$ in [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] makes both maps isomorphisms. Their pullback is therefore isomorphic to $0$ and is quasi-compact. Thus $0$ is quasi-separated, hence coherent by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Quasi-compactness is unchanged by isomorphism: composing a covering family with the isomorphism and its inverse preserves exactly the epimorphic subfamilies. This settles the empty coproduct; when $I=\varnothing$ the assertion indexed by $i\in I$ is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0GMQ, lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact, with its empty-family extension in lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus; agent argument using strictness of the initial object.

proof.text: Let $A=\coprod_{i\in I}A_i$, let $B\to A$ have quasi-compact source, and fix $i\in I$. Put $B_j=B\times_A A_j$. By [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity], $B\simeq\coprod_j B_j$ and the inclusions $B_j\to B$ are monic and disjoint. Given any jointly epimorphic family $(X_t\to B_i)_{t\in T}$, adjoin the maps $B_j\to B$ for $j\ne i$. The resulting family covers $B$: two maps out of $B$ agreeing on it agree on $B_i$ by the epimorphism $\coprod_tX_t\to B_i$, and agree on every other summand, hence agree on $B$. Quasi-compactness of $B$ [def-trf-coherent-topos] selects a finite subfamily. Pull this subfamily back to $B_i$ using clause (1) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus]. Each chosen $X_t$ pulls back to itself because $B_i\to B$ is monic. Each chosen $B_j$, $j\ne i$, pulls back to $0$ by disjointness; deleting these initial terms does not change right cancellation, since every map from $0$ is unique. The finitely many selected $X_t$ therefore still cover $B_i$. This proves its quasi-compactness, without any condition on the $A_j$.

source.place: Agent finite-summand argument from the quasi-compactness definition preceding Tag 0GMP, lemma-image-of-quasi-compact; universal covers supplied by lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus and disjoint universal coproducts by lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity.

proof.text: Now suppose every $A_i$ is coherent and put $A=\coprod_iA_i$. Their quasi-compactness [def-trf-coherent-topos] and clause (3) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] give quasi-compactness of $A$. For arbitrary quasi-compact $B,C$ with maps to $A$, step 2 makes $B_i=B\times_A A_i$ and $C_i=C\times_A A_i$ quasi-compact. Quasi-separatedness of $A_i$ then gives quasi-compactness of $B_i\times_{A_i}C_i$. Put $P=B\times_A C$, with its common map to $A$. Universality in [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] gives $P\simeq\coprod_i(P\times_A A_i)$. The pullback universal property identifies $P\times_A A_i$ with $B_i\times_{A_i}C_i$: both parametrize a map to $B$, a map to $C$, and a common lift of their map to $A$ to $A_i$; uniqueness of that lift follows from the monic inclusion $A_i\to A$. Clause (3) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] now makes $P$ quasi-compact. This proves quasi-separatedness of $A$, hence its coherence. The empty case was treated in step 1, and no coherent-topos or generating-family hypothesis was used.
